content:
In the ultra-competitive world of e-commerce, the image is queen. La product photography is much more than just an illustration: it has become one of the fundamental pillars of the success of an online business. Over the years, technological change has profoundly transformed the way in which products are presented and perceived by consumers, especially in areas such as modus And the props.

We therefore suggest that you trace this evolution of e-commerce and product photography in this article, from its modest beginnings to the advent of revolutionary new technologies. We'll also look at how consumer expectations have changed over time, and why it's essential to update your automated photo studio in order to remain at the forefront of technology.

The evolution of e-commerce and product photography: a chronology

The evolution of e-commerce over the decades reflects not only technological advances in product photography and the internet, but also changes in expectations And the consumer behaviors. But to fully understand all this, let's go back to the very beginning of the 2000s...

The 2000s: the beginnings of e-commerce and the growing importance of the image

‍

In the early 2000s, with the advent of e-commerce, businesses had to adapt to the need to present their products attractively on emerging online platforms. The first CMS have been adopted to effectively manage online content, including product images, thereby laying the foundation for effective visual presentation.

With e-commerce, we have thus seen a first evolution in product photography, which was previously intended primarily for print use.

In the years that followed, the mid-2000s saw the emergence of Rich Media, offering a more immersive user experience. Unlike static content, Rich Media in fact allows users to interact with content in a variety of ways, such as scrolling, zooming, rotating, playing video, animations, etc.

Consumers have also begun to value more product visuals when shopping online, thus stimulating an evolution towards professional quality photography, adapted to the increasingly competitive e-commerce market.

The end of the 2000s was marked by a growing need for transparency And ofgenuineness on the part of businesses, with an emphasis on the quality of the images presented on e-commerce sites to gain the trust of consumers. Technological advances such asdimmable LED lighting have made it possible to meet these requirements, offering more customizable and energy-efficient options for product photography.

With dimmable LED lighting, it thus becomes possible to control the intensity of the light, adjust the color temperature to match different environments, and even change the direction and angle of lighting to highlight the specific characteristics of the product. Thanks to its dimmability, LED lighting gives you total control over the final visual aspect of product photographs. This advance offers more flexibility to adapt lighting to the needs of each product.

The 2010s: the professionalization of product photography to respond to the evolution of e-commerce

During the 2010s, the clipping products and various retouching has become easier thanks to advances in image editing software. Format support RAW has also offered greater flexibility in image post-processing. CMS have also evolved, offering improved functionalities for the management and presentation of product visuals.

‍

We were then able to see the emergence of video And of theartificial intelligence, which also opened up new possibilities for presenting products online. Thanks to advanced algorithms, it is possible to use artificial intelligence in particular to automatically improve the quality of images, by optimizing brightness, contrast and sharpness. It can also be used to automatically crop products, thus facilitating their integration into various environments and creating flawless visuals... And more recently, we can also use AI to transform photos to 360 degrees of your products in visuals 3D, paving the way for new ways to present your products on your e-commerce site.

In the 2010s, theColor Rendering Index (CRI) has also become an important criterion for guaranteeing accurate and true-to-life product visuals. A now well-established standard in product photography.

Nowadays: the generalization of automated solutions for packshots

Automated photo studios make product photography accessible to a wider range of users, from small businesses to internal marketing departments, including in sectors like wine and spirits. The growth of social networks and the use of smartphones has also reinforced the importance of product visuals optimized for these platforms, stressing the need to evolve with the times.

As you can see, the visual quality has only grown in importance over the years. Today, it is absolutely essential not to repel visitors and to convince them to buy your products. In addition, consumer expectations are increasingly high in terms ofuser experience. To remain competitive in a constantly evolving e-commerce market, companies must therefore invest in modern product photography solutions adapted to new technologies and consumer expectations.

What are consumers' expectations in terms of product photography nowadays, following the evolution of e-commerce?

User experience requirements

Consumer expectations play a central role in the success or failure of an online business. And more than ever, consumers are looking for a shopping experience online that is pleasant, intuitive and convincing. High-quality product visuals are an essential part of the e-commerce user experience.

Consumers especially like the opportunity to see products. From every angle, with a sufficient level of detail to make an informed purchase decision. Images that are clear, well-lit, and that highlight product features are critical to generating consumer interest and trust.

Impact of social networks and mobile

With the proliferation of smartphones and the omnipresence of social networks, the way in which consumers interact with product visuals on an e-commerce site and elsewhere has evolved considerably over the years. So you must optimize your images so that they adapt well to mobiles and that they are quick to charge. They must also adapt to the specific formats and characteristics of the various social networks.

Consumers expect to be able to discover and easily share products on their favorite social networks, a trend that is all to your advantage! Your customers can indeed help you increase the reach and visibility of your products and your e-commerce site. It is therefore up to you to facilitate this sharing process and to take care of the photography of your products so that it is effective and engaging.

Changing expectations for authenticity and transparency

Consumers want to see images True to reality, accurately reflecting the appearance and characteristics of the products offered. Misleading or overly retouched photographs can lead to a loss of trust and discourage consumers from making a purchase. As a result, you need to provide transparent and authentic product visuals to build consumer trust and loyalty.

Consumer expectations in terms of product photography in e-commerce are therefore constantly evolving, fuelled by technological advances. Under these conditions, not evolving your product photography solutions internally can prove to be a Costly error. Indeed, if your product photos are of lower quality than those of your competitors, or if you do not offer features that Internet users are now used to, you risk losing customers.
